correctness.rationale: Proof uses forest leaf-pair rank 2ν, vertex-root saturation via deletion rank, alternating-form splitting, unique even-cycle Pfaffian relation, and finite-field count (q−1)^{|S|−1}; Kirillov orbit cardinalities then give characters for odd q. The prior tree rank formula assumes acyclicity and the cycle formula omits hanging trees. The current rank polynomial adds a correction triggered by essentiality of every selected off-cycle root.

Own current-week double-cone result (item 0bfb5f0d-4fa2-4d41-8769-aa2fc199b3ca) transforms only the graph operation of adjoining two nonadjacent universal vertices; even if it includes isolated unicyclic examples such as the four-cycle, it does not enumerate arbitrary hanging-tree attachments.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The new formula specializes to those prior boundary formulas but also treats all mixed cycle/tree supports and quantifies exact exceptional probability 1/(q−1) on each eligible support. Their statements do not logically yield that classification without additional weighted alternating-form analysis. The general Kirillov method supplies the link from rank strata to characters but does not evaluate them. The earlier double-cone transformation does not subsume the unrestricted unicyclic family, as it changes a graph by a fixed join operation rather than an attachment-sensitive single-cycle graph decomposition.

value.rationale: The character-degree enumeration of graphical groups is an explicitly posed natural problem; all unicyclic graphs constitute a structurally motivated infinite family joining but not reducible to trees and bare cycles. The precise essential-root criterion decides when arbitrary attached trees preserve the unique Pfaffian rank resonance; its correction gives all degrees and multiplicities, including q=2 rank statistics. This is a complete natural family classification rather than a single arbitrary instance.
